Story -------- Mr. Takahashi, the mayor of Takahashi City, decided to draw a map of Takahashi City on the floor of the city hall lobby using colored square tiles. Takahashi City is divided into several wards, and in this map, each ward should be represented as a set of connected tiles of the same color. He commissioned a contractor to create a draft of an accurate map, but the number of tiles to be used was too large, and the budget was exceeded. Mayor Takahashi, who loves graphs, is only interested in the adjacencies between the wards and thinks that the map could be drawn with fewer tiles if information other than adjacencies, such as the shape and size of each ward, is ignored. Please create a map using as few tiles as possible.

Problem Statement -------- Given a map of Takahashi City represented on a grid of $n\times n$ squares. Let $(0,0)$ be the coordinates of the top-left square, and $(i,j)$ be the coordinates of the square located $i$ squares down and $j$ squares to the right from there. The city consists of $m$ wards, and the square of color $c$ ($1\leq c\leq m$) corresponds to the $c$-th ward. The outside of the $n\times n$ squares correspond to the outside of the city and is colored $0$. Two squares are defined as "adjacent" if they share an edge, and a set of squares is defined as "connected" if any two squares can reach each other via adjacent squares. In the given map, for each color c, the set of squares of color c is guaranteed to be connected. Your task is to create a map represented on a grid of $n\times n$ squares that satisfies all of the following conditions. - For every color $c$ ($0\leq c\leq m$), squares of color $c$ must be connected. Input -------- Input is given from Standard Input in the following format. ~~~ $n$ $m$ $c_{0,0}$ $c_{0,1}$ $\cdots$ $c_{0,n-1}$ $\vdots$ $c_{n-1,0}$ $c_{n-1,1}$ $\cdots$ $c_{n-1,n-1}$ ~~~ For all test cases, we fix $n = 50$ and $m = 100$. $c_{i,j}$ is an integer value representing the color of the square at coordinates $(i,j)$ and satisfies $1\leq c_{i,j}\leq m$. /**
 * Construct several bounded sparse corridor seeds from the original contact
 * embedding.  Each start keeps one witness cell for every ward, routes
 * Manhattan corridors through currently unused cells, and is accepted only
 * after
 * full connectivity and exact-adjacency validation.  The original map remains
 * the incumbent fallback whenever no constructed seed is legal.
 */
void dual_graph_corridor_seed_phase(
    const std::vector<std::vector<int>>& initial_grid) {
    const AdjacencyInfo original_required = required_adjacencies;
    const std::vector<std::vector<int>> incumbent = current_grid_state;
    const int incumbent_score = best_score_val;

    std::vector<int> degree(M_FIXED + 1, 0);
    for (int c = 1; c <= M_FIXED; ++c) {
        for (int d = 0; d <= M_FIXED; ++d) {
            if (c != d && original_required.is_adj(c, d)) ++degree[c];
        }
    }

    std::vector<int> order;
    for (int c = 1; c <= M_FIXED; ++c) order.push_back(c);
    std::sort(order.begin(), order.end(), [&](int a, int b) {
        if (degree[a] != degree[b]) return degree[a] > degree[b];
        const bool az = original_required.is_adj(0, a);
        const bool bz = original_required.is_adj(0, b);
        if (az != bz) return az > bz;
        return a < b;
    });

    for (int start = 0; start < 4; ++start) {
        std::vector<std::vector<int>> candidate(
            N_FIXED, std::vector<int>(N_FIXED, 0));
        std::vector<std::vector<unsigned char>> occupied(
            N_FIXED, std::vector<unsigned char>(N_FIXED, 0));

        int attempts = 0;
        int expansions = 0;

        for (int color : order) {
            if (++attempts > 80 || expansions > 1500) break;

            std::vector<std::pair<int, int>> cells;
            for (int r = 0; r < N_FIXED; ++r) {
                for (int c = 0; c < N_FIXED; ++c) {
                    if (initial_grid[r][c] == color)
                        cells.push_back({r, c});
                }
            }
            if (cells.empty()) continue;

            const int offset =
                (start * 17 + color * 31) % static_cast<int>(cells.size());
            std::pair<int, int> seed = cells[offset];

            int best_r = -1, best_c = -1, best_cost = INT_MAX;
            for (auto p : cells) {
                int cost = std::abs(p.first - seed.first) +
                           std::abs(p.second - seed.second);
                if (occupied[p.first][p.second]) cost += 100000;
                if (cost < best_cost) {
                    best_cost = cost;
                    best_r = p.first;
                    best_c = p.second;
                }
            }
            if (best_r < 0) continue;

            int r = best_r, c = best_c;
            candidate[r][c] = color;
            occupied[r][c] = 1;

            /*
             * Add short branches toward original witnesses.  Branches are
             * deliberately stopped at occupied cells, keeping the amount of
             * structural reconstruction bounded.
             */
            for (int d = 0; d <= M_FIXED; ++d) {
                if (d == color || !original_required.is_adj(color, d))
                    continue;

                std::pair<int, int> witness = {-1, -1};
                for (int rr = 0; rr < N_FIXED && witness.first < 0; ++rr) {
                    for (int cc = 0; cc < N_FIXED; ++cc) {
                        if (initial_grid[rr][cc] != d) continue;
                        if (std::abs(rr - r) + std::abs(cc - c) <
                            (witness.first < 0 ? INT_MAX :
                             std::abs(witness.first - r) +
                             std::abs(witness.second - c))) {
                            witness = {rr, cc};
                        }
                    }
                }
                if (witness.first < 0) continue;

                int cr = r, cc = c;
                while ((cr != witness.first || cc != witness.second) &&
                       expansions++ < 1500) {
                    if (cr != witness.first) cr += (cr < witness.first ? 1 : -1);
                    else cc += (cc < witness.second ? 1 : -1);

                    if (candidate[cr][cc] != 0 &&
                        candidate[cr][cc] != color)
                        break;
                    candidate[cr][cc] = color;
                    occupied[cr][cc] = 1;
                }
            }
        }

        if (attempts > 80 || expansions > 1500) continue;
        if (!rebuild_and_validate_candidate(candidate, original_required)) {
            rebuild_and_validate_candidate(incumbent, original_required);
            current_grid_state = incumbent;
            best_score_val = incumbent_score;
            continue;
        }

        const int score = static_cast<int>(cells_by_color[0].size());
        if (score > best_score_val) {
            best_score_val = score;
            best_grid_state = current_grid_state;
        }
    }

    rebuild_and_validate_candidate(best_grid_state, original_required);
}

void solve_main_logic() {
    std::vector<std::vector<int>> initial_grid_from_input(N_FIXED, std::vector<int>(N_FIXED));
    for (int i = 0; i < N_FIXED; ++i) for (int j = 0; j < N_FIXED; ++j) std::cin >> initial_grid_from_input[i][j];
    
    initialize_all_data_structures(initial_grid_from_input);

    dual_graph_corridor_seed_phase(initial_grid_from_input);
